title: Observe tool-bound execs and add per-route JSONL labels for streaming
author: Riley Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers running long-lived streamed calls and tool/function invocations were losing correlation between the API request and downstream tool executions (adapters, subprocesses, external tool runners). This made debugging timeouts and tool errors difficult and reduced the value of per-endpoint metrics.

What this PR does (summary):
- Propagates a stable request_id + trace span id into any tool/function execution context (env vars + process args for tool-runner, and headers for remote tool adapters).
- Ensures every streaming fragment emitted from the API surface includes request_id and route labels so JSONL access logs can be correlated to traces and metrics.
- Adds per-route label enrichment to JSONL access logs and to Prometheus metrics produced by the API gateway, enabling route/model/route_version dimension tagging for latency and error metrics.
- Adds OpenAI-compat shim mappings so x-request-id / traceparent are honored and translated into internal request_id when present.

Key changes:
- runtime/toolrunner/exec.go: thread request_id + trace_span into child process env and command args; added short-lived span handoff logic.
- proxy/streaming/fragment_writer.go: include request_id and route.labels in each fragment envelope; backwards-compatible flag keeps legacy small fragments for older clients.
- observability/jsonl_writer.go: include route.labels map flattened to jsonl fields route_name, model, route_version; safe-serialize for non-string labels.
- metrics/route_labels.go: new helper to translate route config into prometheus label set; applied to endpoint_latency and endpoint_errors counters.
- adapters/openai_shim.ts: read x-request-id / traceparent and map to internal request_id header; update tests.
- test/e2e/tool_correlation_test.go: end-to-end test that fires a streaming request, executes a tool, and asserts logs/metrics contain same request_id.

Testing & CI:
- Unit tests added for toolrunner env injection and JSONL label formatting.
- Integration e2e test validates correlation across the gateway -> tool runner -> jsonl pipeline.
- First CI run failed on lint (ts-lint rule for header ordering); fixed in second commit and reran CI which passed.

Compatibility and rollout:
- Backwards compatible: if clients already send x-request-id or traceparent, we use those; otherwise a new internal request_id is generated. An opt-out feature flag (OBS_LEGACY_FRAGMENT) preserves prior fragment payloads for older clients.
- Rollout plan: feature gated under runtime flag. Gradually enable for 10% of traffic for 48h, validate metrics and increased observability dashboards, then ramp to 100%.
- Rollback: disable flag and redeploy gateway config to stop injecting request ids into fragments; no DB or persistent storage changes.

Notes for operators:
- New Prometheus labels for endpoint metrics will increase cardinality (route_name, model, route_version). We recommend updating scrape/recording rules to aggregate by route_name only where necessary.

Related:
- Linear ENG-9183 (streaming observability improvements)
- Support ticket SUP-4421 (customer debugging for tool hangs)

Checklist:
- [x] Propagate request_id into tool runs
- [x] Add request_id to every stream fragment
- [x] Add per-route JSONL fields and metrics labels
- [x] Add unit and e2e tests
- [x] Update OpenAI-compat shim header handling
